question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit outbound recipient authorization policy for Slack DMs here, and should it be Slack-owned `channels.slack.allowTo` or a shared channel/message-tool policy?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix creates a new public security-sensitive config surface and enforcement boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent API shape.

options.title: Design shared outbound target policy
options.body: Define a generic outbound target policy that Slack can consume so future channels do not grow incompatible recipient allowlist semantics.

options.title: Add Slack-owned allowTo
options.body: Implement a Slack-specific `channels.slack.allowTo` gate for explicit Slack DM targets with docs, schema metadata, and focused tests.

options.title: Keep operator-policy only
options.body: Do not add a new OpenClaw config boundary and continue relying on trusted-operator controls plus existing message action and cross-context policy.

recommendation.title: Design shared outbound target policy
recommendation.body: Define a generic outbound target policy that Slack can consume so future channels do not grow incompatible recipient allowlist semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant shared outbound policy and Slack allowlist history most strongly routes the product/API decision there.
